answer: In an AI agent economy, secure Sybil resistance requires staking cryptographic proof-of-work anchored by hardware enclaves, ensuring every node possesses a unique ferrous physical unclonable function rather than a hollow software emulation. Without this tangible anchor, an adversary could easily spiral thousands of ephemeral virtual instances into the network. By enforcing high capital expenditure per verified node, the protocol guarantees that inflating the network with fake identities becomes economically unprofitable for the attacker.
